title: Light Client Backfill in Prysm
description:
Most beacon nodes today checkpoint-sync, meaning they never process historical states and cannot serve old-period light client data. As adoption grows, supply of historical LC updates decays — threatening bridges and mobile wallets that need to sync from old trusted roots.

I will be presenting how a backfill protocol is designed and implemented in Prysm as part of EPF Cohort 7.  The protocol downloads per-period anchor proofs, exhaustively verifies block coverage to prevent omission attacks, locally re-runs is_better_update to determine canonical best updates, and reconstructs bootstraps — all anchored to already-trusted data via Merkle proofs. Each backfilled period turns the node into a supplier, reversing the supply decay.
abstract: Checkpoint-synced beacon nodes lack historical light client data, and supply decays as the network grows. This talk covers designing and implementing a fork-less backfill protocol in Prysm that lets any node trustlessly reconstruct old-period LC updates and bootstraps by downloading per-period proofs and locally re-running the spec's `is_better_update` ranking.
